umbrella_line: Your exposure is hourly. Manage it in the hours where it lives.

IPP.label: Independent Power Producer
IPP.pain: Merchant wind and solar output is sold into hourly prices it doesn't match: solar is long the midday trough (negative prices, curtailment in CAISO) and short the evening ramp; wind often fades into ERCOT evening scarcity hours. Monthly hedges average away exactly that shape, and node-to-hub basis adds a second layer.
IPP.value_prop: Hourly and daily-peak contracts at the hub let a generator manage shape risk in the specific hours its profile misses, directly and without a broker credit line, alongside existing PPAs and offtakes.
IPP.proof_point: Proof to build: an event recap showing a solar profile against an SP15 duck-curve week (negative midday hours, evening-ramp peak) and how an hourly position settles in each hour; illustrative, with basis risk shown explicitly.
education_topics: Duck curve & negative prices for solar IPPs
Shape vs. basis: what a hub contract does and doesn't cover

STORAGE.label: Battery Storage Operator
STORAGE.pain: A large share of a merchant battery's annual revenue can hinge on a handful of scarcity hours and on the trough-to-ramp spread; revenue is volatile year to year, which complicates financing, tolling and dispatch planning.
STORAGE.value_prop: Hourly contracts let operators manage charge and discharge hours separately, take or hedge a view on specific hours, and smooth merchant revenue, on a venue they access directly and programmatically.
STORAGE.proof_point: Proof to build: replay of the Oct-2 ERCOT Houston event and a CAISO negative-price week showing the intraday spread hour by hour, with how hourly positions settle against real-time prices (illustrative, synthetic data).
education_topics: Valuing the intraday spread: storage and hourly contracts
Duck curve & negative prices for solar IPPs

REP.label: Retail Electric Provider
REP.pain: Fixed-price retail obligations sit on top of index-priced supply. In heat and cold events, load rises exactly when real-time prices spike, so a few hours of scarcity can absorb a meaningful share of a season's retail margin; monthly blocks leave the shape unhedged.
REP.value_prop: Daily-peak and hourly contracts let a retail book manage load-following risk in the days and hours it actually occurs, sized to the forecast, accessed directly rather than through bilateral credit lines.
REP.proof_point: Proof to build: an hour-by-hour recap of the Oct-2 HB_HOUSTON scarcity window for an illustrative 50 MW residential load, showing index cost vs. how a daily-peak position settles (illustrative, gross of fees, synthetic).
education_topics: Sizing a daily-peak position against a load forecast
Writing a hedging policy that includes short-dated contracts

CI_LOAD.label: C&I / Large Load
CI_LOAD.pain: Facilities on index or pass-through supply see budget variance driven by a few extreme hours; finance wants predictability, operations can't always curtail, and the supply contract renewal cycle is too slow to respond.
CI_LOAD.value_prop: Weekly and daily-peak contracts give energy and finance teams a direct, transparent tool for the energy-price component of index exposure, without renegotiating the supply agreement. Not a hedge for capacity, transmission (incl. ERCOT 4CP) or demand charges.
CI_LOAD.proof_point: Proof to build: a one-page 'budget vs. actual' teardown of an illustrative index-priced plant through a PJM winter peak week, separating energy, capacity and transmission costs, with the share a weekly-peak contract relates to.
education_topics: Energy vs. capacity vs. transmission: what you can and can't hedge
Onboarding clinic: completing KYC in one pass

UTILITY.label: Utility / Co-op / Muni
UTILITY.pain: Residual purchases at the hub during winter and summer peaks hit when owned and contracted resources are stretched; hedging policies and board approvals were written for monthly/seasonal products, so short-dated tools fall outside the policy and the approval cycle is long.
UTILITY.value_prop: A regulated, transparent, exchange-traded venue for supplemental short-dated hedging that fits prudence and audit requirements: clear settlement against ISO prices, standardized contracts, and reporting a risk committee can follow.
UTILITY.proof_point: Proof to build: a 'policy-ready' briefing pack for risk committees (contract mechanics, collateral, reporting, controls) plus a PJM/MISO winter-peak recap showing residual-purchase exposure for an illustrative co-op.
education_topics: Writing a hedging policy that includes short-dated contracts
Onboarding clinic: completing KYC in one pass

DATACENTER.label: Data Center Developer
DATACENTER.pain: New, large, flat 24x7 load is energizing in phases into tight markets (ERCOT, PJM). Index exposure grows faster than the energy-risk function around it, and PJM capacity costs have risen sharply on load-growth forecasts.
DATACENTER.value_prop: Weekly and daily contracts give a new energy desk a simple, direct starting tool for the energy-price component of a phased load ramp, before (or alongside) long-term PPAs. Capacity and transmission are out of scope, and we say so.
DATACENTER.proof_point: Proof to build: a phased-ramp exposure model (e.g., 50 MW to 300 MW over 18 months) showing how index energy exposure scales and where weekly-peak contracts relate to it; plus 'Data center load & PJM capacity' explainer.
education_topics: Energy vs. capacity vs. transmission: what you can and can't hedge
Onboarding clinic: completing KYC in one pass

PROP.label: Proprietary Trading Firm
PROP.pain: Short-dated US power volatility has mostly been accessible through OTC relationships, ISO virtual bidding or monthly listed products; there are few venues to trade or make markets in hourly and daily price risk directly and programmatically.
PROP.value_prop: Direct, API-first access to short-dated hub contracts in four ISOs, with historical hourly data to model against and a sandbox to certify in; liquidity provided here is visible and two-sided demand from hedgers grows with each event.
PROP.proof_point: Proof to build: an API quick-start with sandbox certification under one day, and an hourly event library (scarcity, negative-price, winter-peak) for backtesting; spread-vs-active-accounts chart from CEO Weekly.
education_topics: Duck curve & negative prices for solar IPPs

FUND.label: Hedge Fund / Asset Manager
FUND.pain: Weather and load views are hard to express cleanly in power: monthly futures dilute the hours that matter and OTC requires ISDA/credit set-up. Operationally, collateral and pre-trade limits set too tight cause rejected first orders.
FUND.value_prop: Standardized daily and weekly contracts on a CFTC-regulated venue, accessed directly, with drivers (weather, load, generation stack) largely specific to the hub and the hour; operational onboarding that gets limits right before the first order.
FUND.proof_point: Proof to build: a factor note on what drives short-dated hub prices (temperature, load, net load, outages) using the event library, plus a 'first order without a rejection' operational checklist.
education_topics: Margin, limits & a first-order dry run

Industry Conferences.role_in_funnel: Top of funnel for hedger segments (REP, Utility, IPP, Storage) and partner discovery; converts best when paired with a pre-booked meeting list from the Activation Queue and a speaking slot built on a Market Pulse event teardown.
Industry Conferences.primary_kpi: Cost per active account (sourced or meeting-influenced within 120 days)
Industry Conferences.notes: Lagging and lumpy: one conference produces a cohort that is small-n for two quarters. Track meetings booked with in-ICP accounts as the leading indicator; cut any show that produces no funded account in two cycles.

Webinars & Education.role_in_funnel: Mid and bottom of funnel: moves SIGNED to FUNDED to FIRST_TRADE by teaching the product on the attendee's own hub; the onboarding clinic directly targets KYC information-request loops.
Webinars & Education.primary_kpi: Cost per active account; secondary: funded-to-first-trade days for attendees vs. matched non-attendees
Webinars & Education.notes: Most of its value is activation influence, not sourcing; report it as influenced, never summed with sourced. Every session is recorded and cut into short clips for the segment explainer touch (D3 of the activation sequence).

Content & SEO.role_in_funnel: Always-on top of funnel and credibility: Market Pulse event recaps, the hub event library and explainers capture search intent from risk managers right after an event.
Content & SEO.primary_kpi: Cost per active account (first-touch); leading: recap-to-meeting conversion within 14 days
Content & SEO.notes: Compounds slowly; judge on a two-quarter horizon. Every recap carries the compliance footer and is reviewed before publish. No gated content for event recaps; gate only deep guides.

LinkedIn Paid.role_in_funnel: Targeted amplification to named personas in ICP accounts (ABM), mostly to drive webinar registration and recap readership, plus retargeting of funded-not-trading contacts with education content.
LinkedIn Paid.primary_kpi: Cost per active account; leading: cost per in-ICP webinar attendee
LinkedIn Paid.notes: Easy to buy cheap leads that never fund. Restrict audiences to title and company lists from the TAM; never optimize to cost per lead. Pause during grid emergencies.

Partner Referrals.role_in_funnel: High-intent sourcing from energy consultants, ISO-market advisors, retail energy brokers and software vendors whose clients already carry short-dated exposure.
Partner Referrals.primary_kpi: Cost per active account (including referral fees)
Partner Referrals.notes: Typically the best cost per active account but selection-biased (referred firms are ready to trade). Referral economics must comply with exchange and CFTC rules on solicitation; Legal approves every partner agreement.

Outbound Prospecting.role_in_funnel: AE- and SDR-led sourcing into top-scored TAM accounts; volatility-triggered sequences for exposed accounts in QUALIFIED to FIRST_TRADE.
Outbound Prospecting.primary_kpi: Cost per active account (fully loaded rep time); secondary: triggered vs. untriggered 14-day activation
Outbound Prospecting.notes: This is where Market Pulse earns its keep. Measure lift with a rotating holdout of exposed accounts per event, not with before/after comparisons.

Liquidity Partner Intros.role_in_funnel: Sourcing of market makers and prop firms through existing liquidity partners and their networks; supply side of the spread flywheel.
Liquidity Partner Intros.primary_kpi: Spread tightening and two-sided uptime per added active liquidity provider (cost per active account reported separately from hedger channels)
Liquidity Partner Intros.notes: LP volume is reported on its own line everywhere. Do not let this channel's ADV-per-dollar flatter blended marketing ROI; hedger activation is the scarce side.
